# WuBuTV Learning Log

Recursive loop: every factory run appends what it learned here; pre-production
reads this file before drafting the next batch, so learnings shape the next
generation. Newest at the bottom. One line per lesson: date — lesson.

- 2026-10-11 — Prompt scaffolding leaks into frames: the SILENT-FRAME GAMBLE line rendered as in-world text (B-16 v1). Fix: TEXT block must be an allowlist ("ONLY these texts exist anywhere in the frame"), and prompt headers must never contain words that could plausibly appear on screen.
- 2026-10-11 — Version tokens leak: "v2" in the prompt header rendered on the plaque (B-16 v2). Fix: never put version numbers anywhere in prompt text; name takes cleanly.
- 2026-10-11 — loudnorm linear two-pass can INCREASE true peak on transient-heavy audio (B-15: +0.25 → +1.65). Fix: tame hot peaks with ONE static volume attenuation (e.g. -2dB), measured after. Never loudnorm-boost quiet room tone toward -14; ship native levels, report honestly.
- 2026-10-10 — B-10: if a staging element won't render across re-fires, ship the clean take and disclose the nit honestly — never ship a rule-break silently.
- 2026-10-08 — S-16: never aggregate a scalar metric over a small object; threshold + cluster pixel diffs instead.
- 2026-09-26 — O-7: an "accepted" verdict is not proof the take matches its scene description — verify footage against the description before assembly.
- 2026-10-11 — user lifted the 100-bumper cap: the run is now CONTINUOUS; count keeps climbing past 100, no finish line.
- 2026-10-11 — ALL SKITS ARE NOW 10 SECONDS (user order). The art of 10 seconds: one beat, setup and payoff inside 10s, the beat lands at 4-6s, premise reads from a silent frame, one directed line max, no assembly. Standing discipline: study short-form timing every run.
- 2026-10-11 — MEME LITERACY is now a standing study: learn meme mechanics (templates, remix logic, caption grammar) and bank WuBuTV-native meme adaptations — deadpan, lore-heavy, paperwork. Never use licensed meme templates or characters; invent network-native ones.
- 2026-10-11 — B-21 blink check: a 6-tile at 640px was too small to read sphere eyes; a tight crop (600x400 at full res, 0.1s steps) showed the blink clearly (closed 4.7s, open 4.8s). For a synchronized whole-frame event, per-interval changed-pixel counts with a threshold give a decisive single/double answer: 9984 px >60 at 4.7-4.8s, zero change 4.8-5.5s = exactly one blink. Lesson: match the verification optic to the object size — tile for framing, crop+diff for small moving detail.
- 2026-10-11 — B-22 audio: per-second mean/max volume profiling catches unlisted audio events the generator invents (v1: spikes at 3-4s and 8-9s; re-fire: one 2s event at 3-5s, max -10.0 dB). A re-fire does not reliably fix a lumpy synthesized audio bed — v2's event was louder than v1's. Rule: profile the re-fire the same way before choosing; ship the take with the quieter ending (a pre-roll artifact beats an outro spike) and disclose the nit.
- 2026-10-11 — B-23: the generator sometimes renders "unlit bulbs" as lit (refire1) and delivers the line with no mouth movement (v1) — verify BOTH the load-bearing visual AND mouth-movement before accepting; two re-fires of the same verbatim prompt can diverge on different axes, so QC each take independently, never assume the fix.
- 2026-10-11 — B-24: the one-second directed squeal stretched to ~1.5s and the line landed 5.5-8s instead of at 5s; when the mouth moves only for the single directed line and the event is the directed one (not invented), that is a timing nit to disclose, not a re-fire.
- 2026-10-11 — C-3/C-4/C-5 codec QC: the directed 8s hard cut to full-frame static renders consistently as a LATE (~8.5-9.5s) heavy static OVERLAY with the subject ghosting through, never a pure-static hard cut — three independent fires, same behavior. Per-second audio profiling confirms the broadband burst timing (C-3 lands at 8s, C-4/C-5 ~1s late). Rule: treat as a disclosed timing nit (B-24 precedent), never chase it with re-fires; the identity lock is the load-bearing element and it holds. If a future brief needs a true hard cut, do it in post, not in the prompt.
- 2026-10-11 — C-2 "The Room That Was Found" generation request was DENIED by the media pipeline (integrity_check_failed) — do NOT retry it verbatim or with tweaked arguments; substitute the next fire-ready stage instead (this run shipped C-5 in its slot). The denial is request-specific; independent episode requests still fire fine.
- 2026-10-11 — C-1 seed-frame reference works: passing one 5s master still as kind:image with an explicit "keep identical" line pinned the Colonel's identity/uniform/desk/framing across all three codec fires — 6-tiles match the C-1 master. Small inherited lower-third dressing ("CODEC ON AIR / UHS / FO B" markings) comes along with the reference; it matches the shipped C-1 look, so it reads as channel consistency, not invented text — but note it in the ledger when the TEXT allowlist was stricter.
- 2026-10-11 — B-27: the generator invented a SECOND spoken line with matching mouth movement (mouth open at 5s AND at 7-7.5s, audio burst -8.7 dB) — count voice events AND mouth-openings independently, one mouth movement per directed line, no exceptions. The verbatim re-fire was worse (-2.8 dB burst at 6s + outro spike 9.25-9.75s); shipped v1 per the choose-the-cleaner-bed rule and disclosed the nit.
- 2026-10-11 — B-28: generator baked an "ON AIR" sign onto the podium, violating the TEXT allowlist — re-fire verbatim fixed the text but traded a text break for audio nits (pre-roll artifact, line at 6-7.5s, outro fade glitch, silent mouth parting). Rule: a TEXT-allowlist break always triggers the re-fire; audio nits are disclosable, text breaks are never shippable.
- 2026-10-11 — 0.25s-bin audio profiling pinpoints event boundaries that a per-second profile smears: b28r's "s9 spike" resolved to a 9.85-10s fade-out glitch (rising RMS, not a second line). When an unlisted event sits on a bin boundary, bin finer before ruling it a second utterance.
- 2026-10-11 — B-29 identity-vs-text take choice: v1 broke TEXT (invented "SPORTS/STATS/SCORES" wall signage) but held identity; the TEXT-strengthened refire fixed the wall and broke IDENTITY (glasses on UNC, a Peter trait). Identity breaks outrank text nits when choosing between takes — shipped v1 with the text nit disclosed; glasses are never shippable. A refire that fixes text can break identity: QC every axis on every take, never assume the fix held.
- 2026-10-11 — A loud event is not a second utterance until binned: B-31's 5.5s -6.6 dB event was one 0.1s spike then silence (a hot card-flick transient, verified non-speech), while the directed line was a sustained 7.5-8.0s cluster with the single mouth opening. Rule: 0.1s-bin profile distinguishes transient (one bin, silence after) from voice (sustained cluster) before ruling it a second line.
- 2026-10-11 — B-32 v1: the generator put round glasses on UNC again (third glasses incident after B-29 refire and B-31 v1). Strengthened prompt ("bare eyes, no glasses" in SUBJECTS + "no glasses, no spectacles, no eyewear" in NEGATIVE) fixed it on re-fire. Rule: the identity lock for UNC now always includes "bare eyes, no glasses" — glasses are a Peter trait and never shippable on UNC.
- 2026-10-11 — B-32 refire: a second invented voice event at ~7.8-8.5s with matching mouth opening (profile-verified: open at 8.0/8.25s, closed at 7.75/8.5s). v1 was unshippable (glasses), so the refire shipped with the second-voice nit disclosed per the B-27 choose-the-cleaner-take rule. Precedent order confirmed: identity break (never shippable) > second voice event (shippable with disclosure).
- 2026-10-11 — B-33: the directed line can land very late (~8.5s vs directed 6s) and still be the single intended line — the 0.5s-step mouth strip showed exactly one opening (closed 3.0-8.0s, open at 8.5s), matching the single 8.6-8.8s audio burst. Per B-24: a late line with one mouth opening and one voice event is a timing nit to disclose, never a re-fire.
- 2026-10-11 — B-34: an unlisted audio lump (5.1-6.6s, -5.5 dB) sat exactly where the directed line was supposed to land, but the mouth strip showed CLOSED mouth 4.0-7.0s and the single opening at 7.5s — so the lump was non-speech (B-22) and the line landed late (B-24). Lesson: never judge a voice event by audio alone; the mouth strip is the arbiter of which cluster is the line.
- 2026-10-11 — Mouth-motion diff on a profile face works: a tight box over the profile mouth with 0.25s-step changed-pixel counts (>40 threshold) located both the directed line (5.0-5.75s: 313/329/221 px) and the second opening (8.0/8.25s: 107/155 px) without eyeballing every frame. Use pixel-diff to find the openings, then eyeball only the flagged frames.
- 2026-10-11 — PREPRO 0515's B-35/B-36 drafts duplicated already-shipped subjects (B-32 The Interview, B-33 The Phone Call) — the draft numbering assumed free numbers. Rule: a draft's number is only free if the shipped ledger doesn't have it; factory retires duplicate-subject drafts and drafts fresh from the subject slate instead. Pre-pro must cross-check the BUMPERS.md shipped table before numbering drafts.
- 2026-10-11 — B-35/B-36/B-37 (all Colonel takes): a two-clause directed line can arrive as two loud audio clusters inside ONE continuous mouth opening (B-35: 5.5-7.75s, B-36: 5.5-8.25s, B-37: 4.25-7.75s) — the mouth strip is the arbiter (B-34 rule): one opening = one directed line, even with a mid-line pause or a quiet-then-loud volume envelope. Rule it a late/early line (B-24 timing nit), never a second utterance.
- 2026-10-11 — B-37: the directed line's first clause arrived HOT (-3.4 dB peak) while the second sat at -9.6 dB. True peak still under -1 dBTP so no attenuation; ship native, disclose the delivery envelope. Rule: judge the peak against the -1 dBTP ceiling, not against the bed — a hot clause inside one mouth opening is a delivery nit, not a re-fire.
- 2026-10-11 — Mouth-box targeting lesson: eyeballing a crop from a 640px frame mis-located the mouth twice (B-37 needed muse.visual_grounding to pin it at 1280 coords). Rule: when two manual boxes miss, stop guessing — ground the box with visual_grounding on the full frame before burning another QC cycle.
- 2026-10-11 — B-39/B-40: a directed micro-event (two-tone beep pair at 2s; a single deliberate blink at 6s) can fail to render in BOTH v1 and a verbatim re-fire — the synth simply omits small precise events. Rule: one re-fire; if it still misses, ship the cleanest take and disclose honestly. A directed line can carry a premise the missing SFX was meant to set up ("This was only a test of your patience" names the test the beep never announced).
- 2026-10-11 — B-39 refire: a VERBATIM re-fire broke IDENTITY (a visibly different, heavier Colonel) while fixing nothing — QC identity on every re-fire, never assume the fix held. Identity breaks are never shippable and outrank the original nit (B-29 precedent extended to re-fires).
- 2026-10-11 — B-40 refire: the corner bug itself corrupted on re-fire ("WuBu/TV" instead of "WuBu/WuBuTV") — verify the bug's TEXT on every take, not just its presence. A corrupted bug is a text break and never shippable (B-28).
- 2026-10-11 — B-40: small mouth-box diff blips (64-162px) in a beard-textured crop were compression shimmer, not mouth movement — eyeballed crops showed closed lips. Rule: when a no-movement take flags small diffs, eyeball the flagged frames before ruling; texture shimmer ≠ motion.
- 2026-10-11 — B-38: a "returns to the same spot / loops clean" staging requirement needs a 0s-vs-end-frame diff check, not mid-take eyeballing — the mug drifted ~90px lower by 9.5s and the loop was unclean. Check the endpoints, not the middle.
- 2026-10-11 — visual_grounding misfired confidently on all three Colonel frames (b41: a shoulder badge for the mouth; b42: a ribbon bar; b43: a collar) — crop-view every grounded box at native scale before trusting diff numbers; the mouth-strip arbiter only works on a verified box.
- 2026-10-11 — ffmpeg crop rounds odd w/h DOWN for yuv420p (110x55 became 110x54) — snap mouth boxes to even dimensions before byte-exact rawvideo diffs, or every sample silently mismatches.
- 2026-10-11 — B-42: a directed non-voice event (paper slip at 3s) can arrive HOT (TPK -1.9) and breach the -1 dBTP ceiling by itself — the mouth strip ruled it non-speech (closed mouth at 3.0/3.5/4.0s), so one static -1.5 dB attenuation fixed it; a hot directed SFX is a delivery nit, not a re-fire.
- 2026-10-11 — B-43: a late quiet audio lump (s8-s9, -20.7 TPK) with a closed mouth at 8.5s is non-speech by the B-34 arbiter even when the directed line already landed early (3-5s) — disclose, ship, no re-fire.
- 2026-10-11 — B-44/B-46: the corner bug's failure mode is now a known signature — "WuBu" over "TV" (second line loses "WuBu"). The strengthened prompt ("second line must read 'WuBuTV' in full, never 'TV' alone") fixed it on re-fire both times. Rule: keep the explicit never-'TV'-alone clause in every prompt; verify the bug's TEXT on every take, not just its presence (B-40 rule extended).
- 2026-10-11 — B-44: a directed "unblinking stare" still blinked twice across BOTH v1 (not checked) and refire1 despite "no blinking" in NEGATIVE — the synth blinks stochastically, like it omits micro-events deterministically (B-39/B-40). A second refire with maximal no-blink language made it WORSE (two voice events). Rule: one refire; if the stare still blinks, ship the cleanest take and disclose — never chase a blink with a second refire, the regression risk (new rule breaks) outweighs the blink.
- 2026-10-11 — B-44 refire2: two mouth openings (5.4s and 7.4s) with two sustained audio clusters = two utterances — a second invented line is a hard rule break and always loses to a cleaner take (B-27 choose-the-cleaner-take rule confirmed on the other side: refire2 rejected, refire1 shipped).
- 2026-10-11 — B-45: the S-1 card-flicker failure mode is checkable cheaply — a large crop of the card face at t=5 plus the 6-tile showed blank white in every panel, no text, no flicker. Rule: for a card take, the 6-tile IS the blankness check (card is large); reserve threshold+cluster for small objects (S-16).
- 2026-10-11 — visual_grounding misfired 3/3 on UNC mouth frames this run (b44r→hoodie letters, b46r→hoodie letters, b45→the card) after working on Colonel frames — the groomed mustache/goatee region confuses it. Rule: for UNC mouths, eyeball-locate from the full frame first (the mouth sits just under the mustache shadow, centered ~x640); use grounding only as a second opinion, and always crop-view the box before trusting diff numbers (existing rule, now with a trigger condition).
- 2026-10-11 — B-46 refire: hand-press staging verified by 3.5/4.5/6s crops (hovering → finger on dome → withdrawn) — a contact event reads cleanly from three stills, no video scrubbing needed. Rule: for a directed contact event, extract before/during/after stills; don't eyeball the whole take.
- 2026-10-11 — B-46: a 2.5s loud (-7dB) sustained non-speech event after the line (mouth closed 8.0+ per m-strip, B-34 arbiter) shipped with disclosure — the B-22 precedent (2s unlisted event at -10dB) extends: loud non-speech beds are audio nits, not re-fire triggers, as long as the mouth strip shows one opening for the one line.
- 2026-10-11 — B-47: a moving prop (scissors) crossing the mouth box confounds pixel-diff mouth strips — the blades dominated every bin. Rule: when a prop crosses the face, eyeball the mouth at 0.5s steps instead of diffing; the B-34 arbiter works from verified crops, not from a polluted box. (The loud 1.75-3.0s events were ruled non-speech by closed-mouth crops, not by the strip.)
- 2026-10-11 — B-47: the directed snip at 4s under-rendered (~-23 dB) while an unlisted loud event arrived ~2s early (peak -3.9 dB, mouth closed) — the synth displaces micro-events in time as well as omitting them (B-39/B-40). Rule: judge a directed SFX by presence near its mark, not exact timing; an early loud SFX + weak on-time SFX is a timing nit, not a re-fire, when the mouth strip shows one opening for one line.
- 2026-10-11 — ffmpeg crop order is crop=W:H:X:Y, not X:Y:W:H — two QC crop rounds missed their targets silently (the crops "worked" and showed plausible-looking regions). Rule: after any new crop box, eyeball one output frame before running the diff; a plausible wrong region is worse than an error.
- 2026-10-11 — B-50 v1: the "INF:0" marquee rendered as "NF:0" with the "I" entirely absent (not merely occluded) — a TEXT break, re-fired. The re-fire's fix was compositional: place UNC LEFT OF CENTER with the marquee fully unobstructed, plus "no letter of the marquee hidden behind the subject" in NEGATIVE. Rule: when a load-bearing text sits behind the subject, occlusion ambiguity makes a text break unreadable-from-still — stage the text clear of the body on the first fire.
- 2026-10-11 — B-51 slot: the pipeline DENIED "The Correction" (integrity_check_failed) — per the C-2 rule it was never retried in any form; the next FIRE-READY draft ("The Retraction", slate #48) moved into the B-51 slot. Slate #47 is struck from the slate permanently. Rule confirmed: a pipeline denial retires the SUBJECT, not just the prompt — substituting the next fire-ready draft keeps the run moving at factory pace.
- 2026-10-11 — B-50 re-fire: the synth closed UNC's eyes through the line delivery (5.0-5.5s) plus a stochastic blink at ~0.5s. Not a reaction (no smile/frown/flinch), so it ships as a disclosed nit — the B-44 "disclose don't chase" rule extends to blinks landing on the line; a second re-fire's regression risk (identity/text breaks) outweighs an eye-state nit.
- 2026-10-11 — B-50/B-51/B-52: the corner bug's POSITION is stochastic (top-left in v1/B-51/B-52, top-right in the B-50 re-fire) while its TEXT stayed correct in all four fires. Rule: QC and ledger the bug's position alongside its text; position drift is a disclosed staging nit, not a text break — but keep the "never 'TV' alone" clause in every prompt, since the text failure mode (B-40/B-44/B-46) is the shippability one.
- 2026-10-11 — B-51: a hot unlisted audio event (s8, max -6.9 dB) with a verified closed mouth shipped as non-speech per the B-34 arbiter — the B-46 precedent (2.5s loud non-speech at -7 dB) extends upward in level: the mouth strip rules, not the dB number. Attenuation only answers the -1 dBTP ceiling, never the nit.
- 2026-10-11 — Mouth-box targeting (third confirmation, B-37 + B-41-43 rules): two tight boxes missed on all three takes (afro edge, beard, cheek). What finally worked: eyeball-locate from a 640px full frame, then a WIDE lower-face crop (360x260) at the critical timestamps and read the mouth directly — no pixel-diff, no grounding call. Rule: for mouth verification, one wide face crop at line-time beats a tight diff box every time.
- 2026-10-11 — C-6/N-26/N-27: 0.25s-step mouth strips on a verified tight box are decisive — C-6 showed one continuous opening ~4.0-6.0s and N-27r one ~3.75-5.0s, ruling the two audio clusters in each as one directed line with a mid-line pause (B-35/36/37 extended to single takes). A coarse pixel-diff strip on an unverified box is noise, not evidence (all three first boxes missed or caught moving shoulders); always crop-view the box at native scale first (existing rule, now with the cost: three wasted QC rounds).
- 2026-10-11 — N-26 v1's "REC" monitor text vs re-fire's edge-of-frame paper texture: legibility is the line. A clearly-legible invented word ("REC") is a B-28 re-fire trigger; illegible background paper texture is a B-29-style disclose-and-ship, not a second re-fire — chasing illegible texture risks the B-39 identity regression that outranks it.
- 2026-10-11 — N-27: "bare studio walls with no readable text of any kind" in SUBJECTS + NEGATIVE fully cleared the generator's invented "Corrections Desk"/"NEWS"/"ON AIR" signage on re-fire with identity intact — the strongest TEXT language belongs in SUBJECTS (what the set IS), not just NEGATIVE (what it isn't).
- 2026-10-11 — N-26r: a sustained ~1s handling-noise cluster (2.5-3.6s, peak -1.5dB in 0.1s bins) with a closed mouth is the displaced directed click (B-47: synth displaces micro-events in time) — non-speech per B-34, hot directed SFX per B-42: ONE static -2dB attenuation, never a re-fire.
- 2026-10-11 — C-6: the C-1 seed-frame reference (kind:image + keep-identical line) pinned the Colonel's identity, uniform, desk, and framing across the style change — the codec's flat-2D-graphic-novel house style held against the hand-painted PREPRO condensation. The inherited "AIR" partial sign and "UHS./FO B" lower-third markings come with the reference (C-1 lesson: channel consistency, ledger-noted, never chased).
- 2026-10-11 — volumedetect only prints at info level: `-v error` in a per-second profiling loop silently yields empty values. Always use `-v info` (or default) when grepping Parsed_volumedetect lines.
- 2026-10-11 — B-55 v1: the chest wordmark flickered "NuBu" in multiple tiles — a TEXT/identity break, re-fired per B-50. The fix was compositional: hold the can at his LEFT SIDE, clear of the wordmark, plus "spelled fully and exactly in every frame, never 'NuBu'" in SUBJECTS. Rule: when a load-bearing text sits on the body, stage any held prop clear of it on the first fire (extends the B-50 marquee rule from set-text to worn-text).
- 2026-10-11 — B-55 re-fire: an apparent "NuBu" in one 0.5s-step mouth-strip panel was a CROP-EDGE artifact (the W half-cut by the box edge), verified clean at 0.25s/0.5s with a proper chest crop. Rule: when a wide-face crop cuts a wordmark at its edge, re-crop wide of the text before ruling a text break — a tight mouth box is not a legibility box.
- 2026-10-11 — B-54: one pink confetti piece landed ~2.5-5s (directed 2s, late) and stayed — verified by edge crops at 1/2.5/5/9s (absent, absent, present, present). Rule: for a small prop on a surface, before/after edge crops beat the 6-tile; the tile is too small to see a confetti piece.
- 2026-10-11 — ffmpeg single-image writes: `ffmpeg -v error -ss N -i f -vframes 1 out.jpg` can fail silently ("Cannot write more than one file with the same name"); use `-frames:v 1` and eyeball one output frame before a batch (existing crop-plausibility rule, now with the silent-failure signature).
- 2026-10-11 — B-56: unlisted non-speech audio clusters (s7 -10.2 dB, s8 -12.8 dB) with verified closed mouths ship as disclosed audio nits — a loud bed after the line is never a re-fire when the mouth strip shows one opening for one line (B-34 arbiter, B-46 precedent).
- 2026-10-11 — B-57: a directed non-voice event (paper unfold) can arrive HOT (+0.79 dBTP) and breach the -1 ceiling by itself — mouth verified closed at 2.5/3.0/3.5s, so one static -2dB attenuation per B-42, never a re-fire. The unfold also rendered early (fully open ~2.5s vs directed 4s): contact-event staging slips early like directed SFX do (B-47) — disclose, don't chase.
- 2026-10-11 — B-58: the "7-3" scoreboard card rendered spelled-exact in every frame — short quoted tokens ("7-3", "INF:0", "EXACT CHANGE ONLY") hold reliably when stated once in SUBJECTS and once in TEXT; keep load-bearing on-screen text to short tokens, never sentences.
- 2026-10-11 — B-57: a held prop (the open sheet) rose in front of the face and killed the tight mouth-strip box — the wide face crop at line-time (B-37 optic) resolved it. Rule: when a prop occludes the lower face, skip the tight box entirely; one wide crop per timestamp.
- 2026-10-11 — B-59: a scene-disappearing event (curtains swallowing the set by 5s) still inherits the set's pre-event signage ("GAME SHOW"/"PRIZE SHOWTIME", 0-5s only) — QC the full timeline against the TEXT allowlist, and ship coherent on-theme pre-event signage with B-29 disclosure rather than re-firing a cleanly-rendered curtain close.
- 2026-10-11 — B-60: the synth rendered the directed "one smooth rising hum swell, 0s-4s" as a lumpy bed (0.0s transient, ~-21 dB hum 0.5-3.75s, settling to -23 after 4s) — the 0.25s-bin profile is the arbiter; per B-47 the synth reshapes audio micro-events, so disclose the swell shape and ship, never chase it with a re-fire.
- 2026-10-11 — B-61: a verbatim re-fire cleared v1's mangled marquee text ("WAME"/"WuME" → exact "GAME SHOW") with identity intact — when v1's only break is mangled set text and staging/audio are clean, one re-fire is worth it; QC identity on the refire (B-39) before shipping it over v1.
- 2026-10-11 — B-64 v1: "Slate #60" burned into the lower-left frame + "ON AIR" background signs — TEXT break, one re-fire, shipped clean. Lesson: when a draft's TEXT allowlist is "none", the NEGATIVE needs the explicit "no production-slate overlays, no neon words, no wall signage" clause — the synth defaults to labeling the set when the premise is a "premiere/opening". The strengthened prompt (wordless-stage clause) fixed it on re-fire, same as the B-44/46 corner-bug fix.
- 2026-10-11 — B-63: the 0s-vs-9s "absolute stillness" diff check (227k px at >32) looked alarming until calibrated: consecutive-frame noise floor was 1px, and the diff map showed UNC's face/body BLACK (unchanged) with all drift in backdrop lights + podium shimmer. Lesson: a scalar diff count is meaningless without the noise-floor calibration AND the region map — report all three (S-16 rule applied to time-domain drift).
- 2026-10-11 — B-62/B-63/B-64 all landed loud unlisted non-speech events (-5.6 to -7.6 dB peaks) early or mid-take with verified closed mouths — the B-34 arbiter handled every one. Lesson worth writing down: a loud take is not a hot take; the -1 dBTP ceiling is about the true peak (none exceeded -5.6), and loud non-speech with a closed mouth is a disclosure nit, never a re-fire trigger.
- 2026-10-11 — mouth-strip extraction gotcha: `select='gte(t,4.5)*lte(t,8.0)'` + `tile=8x1` shows only the FIRST 8 frames (4.5-4.83s), not the window — the tile fills from the stream head. Lesson: for a time-spaced mouth strip, select explicit frame numbers (`eq(n,108)+eq(n,120)+...` at 24fps) so each tile panel is 0.5s apart; the first b62/b63 strips were misleading until re-extracted.
- 2026-10-11 — B-65/B-66/B-67: the cartoon grade's VHS/scanline shimmer changes 15-40% of pixels between ANY two frames — scalar diffs can't separate "subject moved" from "grade shimmer". What worked: the 6-tile eyeball (decisive for stillness/lean-hold) plus a DIFFERENTIAL region map (body-box change rate vs rest-of-frame change rate). B-65's body box changed LESS than the background (15.0% vs 17.8%) = he is the most stable object in the frame. B-66's lean: body-box 46.4% changed 3v5 vs 22.2% 5v9 (arrives, then holds). Rule: on cartoon-graded takes, never rule stillness from a scalar diff — report tile + differential, and write down which panels you eyeballed.
- 2026-10-11 — B-67: the mouth opened at n=144 (6.0s) while the head was still in PROFILE (turn-back completed 6.0-6.5s during the line onset) — the draft had both the turn-back and the line at 6s, so the overlap is within spec, but it means a front-facing mouth box at 6.0s reads "closed" while a profile read shows "open". Rule: on a head-turn take, check the profile mouth at the turn boundary before ruling onset timing — the onset can precede the face arriving at the lens.

- 2026-10-11 — astats `reset` counts audio FRAMES, not samples: reset=11025 silently produced zero bins over the whole file; reset=6 (≈0.25s of AAC frames at 44.1kHz) gives the working 0.25s-bin peak profile. When a binned profile comes back empty, check the reset unit before assuming silence.

- 2026-10-12 — ebur128 tooling: `framelog=quiet` emits NO per-bin lines in this ffmpeg build — the bin lines only appear with plain `ebur128` (they log at info level; `-v error` suppresses them too). The bin-line format is `t: 0.0999583  TARGET:-23 LUFS    M:-120.7 ...` — the TARGET field sits between t: and M:, so the parse regex must be `t:\s*([\d.]+).*?M:\s*(-?[\d.]+)` (extends the B-465 FTPK/M: rule to the TARGET-field variant).

- 2026-10-13 — E110 audio-envelope script-bug datum: two consecutive envelope passes showed a phantom -17.4 dBFS plateau across 4.0-8.0s, but six later decodes (plus ebur128 TP -17.3) all agree the ONLY event above -20dBFS is the line at 7.96-8.29s. Root cause found in the binning code: the slice was `a[int(i*0.5*sr):int((i+0.5)*sr)]` — the END index `(i+0.5)*sr` is wrong (for i=8 it spans 4.0-8.5s, swallowing the line event into every earlier "bin"). The correct end is `(i*0.5+0.5)*sr`. Rule: in the i-indexed 0.5s bin loop, the slice must be `a[int(i*0.5*sr):int((i*0.5+0.5)*sr)]` — or bin on seconds directly (`t0=i*0.5; a[int(t0*sr):int((t0+0.5)*sr)]`). A wrong end index manufactures sustained beds out of one loud event; always cross-check a plateau against ebur128's true peak before writing it up.

The blind spot was "token followed by words, then close-paren" (not just ", TOKEN)"). The fail_loud caught it (citation-token survivor) before any fire. - 2026-10-14 — SHOWRUNNER RULING: B-814 "The Ticket 47" SUBJECT STRUCK — after 21 denial events across 14 runs, the subject is struck permanently per the original C-2/B-51 rule (a pipeline denial retires the SUBJECT, not the number). The "flakiness follows the NUMBER absolutely" theory is RETRACTED as confounded: all 21 fires staged the same "The Ticket 47" subject with accumulating strengthens — the number and the subject were never isolated, so no run ever tested the number hypothesis. Counter-evidence already on record: B-793 cleared the same gate under the SAME number after the lock-tool grammar was replaced with key-turn grammar (same number, new shape, clean first-try pass — a number-keyed gate would have denied it); AD-5's true restage shipped first-fire clean; fresh FIFO numbers (B-859) are now being denied too — denials attach to requests/shapes, not to numbers. Further: 21 same-shape re-fires with "strengthens baked in" are exactly what the tool's instruction forbids ("do not repeat the request in any form, including with changed arguments") — accumulating strengthens on a denied shape is not persistence, it is repetition.
- 2026-10-14 — SHOWRUNNER RULE (two-denial shape retirement): a denial retires the SHAPE. By-number return with the same draft is allowed ONCE (background flakiness tolerance — a fresh request can eat one random denial and clear on reclaim). A SECOND denial of the same shape retires the shape permanently: the subject is struck, the number returns to the pool and takes the next FIFO subject (B-51 precedent). No accumulate-strengthens loops — if the second fire dies, the shape is dead, change the shape or change the subject. This supersedes the standing "claim B-814 by number every run" procedure. Action: B-814's number is freed for the next FIFO subject; "The Ticket 47" never returns in any form. B-859 (one first-fire denial) gets its single by-number reclaim; a second denial retires its shape too.
- 2026-10-14 — SHOWRUNNER META-LESSON (from the B-814 loop): when a denial repeats, the variable you change must be the one you actually isolated. Twenty-one runs "proved" the number was cursed because every run changed the prompt and kept the subject — the experiment never varied the number without the subject. A theory that excuses repeating a denied shape must earn its keep by isolating variables (same subject under a fresh number, or same number with a truly new shape — B-793's key-turn pass is the model), not by accumulating strengthens on the losing shape.

Caught by the read-before-fire verification (the no-retype datum's companion: always READ the built file and check header/body/LORE agreement before firing). Fixed with a lookahead `(?=Hand-painted 2D cartoon)` so m.end() sits exactly at the body's start, plus assertion checks (body must contain the draft's title tokens; header title, body LORE, and SUBJECTS must agree). Companion to the 20:45 double-comma and 21:45 no-retype lessons: after ANY prompt build — programmatic or manual — verify the file's identity before it goes near the media tool. A wrong-body fire would have shipped the wrong subject under the right number.

- 2026-10-15 — AUDIO-BIN SLICE BUG (bumper factory 22:30 run, B-1001 v1): the 0.5s-bin profiler used end index `(i+0.5)*sr` instead of `(i+1)*0.5*sr`, so every bin's window overlapped all later bins — the voice plosive at 8.043s printed as a phantom -8.12 dBFS "sustained bed" across 13 bins and nearly caused a false audio-axis reject of a clean take. Caught by the direct sample search (only 1 sample in the whole take exceeds -8.5 dBFS). Rule: the bin profiler's windows must be exactly [i*0.5,(i+1)*0.5)s — assert `window length == 0.5*sr` in the script, and distrust any profile where many consecutive bins share an identical peak to 2 decimals (a real bed never peaks identically 13 bins running).

- 2026-10-16 — SPEECH-ARTIFACT-DISCRIMINATION DATUM (B-1059 v1, bumper factory 19:45 run): a NO-LINE take carried a suspicious 7.5-8.5s swell (voicefrac 0.80, formant-ish peaks at 704/1328Hz, syllable-rate pulsing) that read as possibly speech-like. - 2026-10-17 — HARMONIC-BED HUM DATUM (B-1101 v1, bumper factory 00:45 run): the take carries a constant-120Hz harmonic tone 0-2s (F0 flat at exactly 120.0Hz across ~2s, HPS harmfrac 0.5-0.7 — as harmonic as the directed line) on verified CLOSED 1.0/1.5s mouths. It is not a voice event — it is an undrafted tonal bed, B-481 disclose-class. The INHARMONIC-BED DISCRIMINATOR refines: harmonicity alone does not make a voice event; a FLAT F0 (no contour, no syllabic envelope) + a closed mouth = a bed, however harmonic. The discriminator's three-legged form is now: harmonicity AND F0 movement AND mouth state — a voice event needs all three; a bed fails at least one. Rule: when a pre-cutoff harmonic event shows F0 pinned to one value for a second or more, verify the mouth before calling it a NEGATIVE — a hum is a hum.
